analysis.title: Weekly Headings (Investment Strategy), November 20, 2026
key_insights: The S&P 500 is on track for its fifth decline in six weeks and its steepest weekly loss (~5%) since April 2025, leaving the index ~8% below its highs. The report says this year's largest drawdown is ~9%, so no 10% correction has occurred in 2026.

3Q S&P 500 EPS growth was 31% YoY and the forward P/E has fallen to its lowest level since 2023. The S&P 500's 14-day RSI of 31 is approaching oversold territory. Raymond James reads these as reasons the pullback may offer opportunities for disciplined investors.

37% of S&P 500 stocks are in bear market territory (down at least 20% from 52-week highs). The average Technology stock is down 33% with 73% of the sector in a bear market, and Communication Services is down 28% with 58% in a bear market.

The 10-year real yield rose nearly 30 bps in two weeks while the 10-year breakeven fell ~10 bps to its lowest since Sept. 2024. The 10-year yield's climb back above 5% has been driven entirely by real rates, as markets price a more hawkish Fed path.

Since the 10-year yield topped 5%, all eight daily S&P 500 declines of more than 1% coincided with falling yields, averaging a five bp drop. From March through the summer, similar equity declines pushed yields five bps higher on average, so Treasuries are again acting as a hedge.

The US Dollar Index is at its highest since March 2025 and on pace for its sixth straight quarterly gain. Markets price more than three Fed rate hikes by June 2027, and Raymond James expects a December hike followed by an extended pause, so it sees the dollar's jump as possibly stretched.

Within the Dollar Index basket the Swedish krona is down the most YTD on a dovish central bank. The euro is down sharply despite ECB hawkishness on French budget deficit and April presidential election concerns. The yen has held up better on multiple government interventions.
October retail sales rose 0.2% MoM, held back by autos and furniture, while control group sales rose 0.6% with upward revisions to prior months.
Pending home sales fell 4.7% MoM to a record low for the second month in a row. Housing starts rose 9.9% on a 25.5% jump in multifamily, but building permits fell 7.4% to their lowest since May 2020.
Raymond James expects headline and core PCE to accelerate to 3.75% and 3.2% YoY, with PCE and the Beige Book both due Wednesday.

The Commerce Department introduced export controls restricting China-linked companies' remote access to advanced US computing capacity through overseas data centers and third-country intermediaries. It also added licensing for certain chip shipments to five countries identified as diversion routes.

The report's top-ten list cites: S&P 500 EPS growth above 30% in 2026, jobless claims at or below 200k for nine straight weeks, retail sales up more than 6% YoY in October, and hyperscaler AI spending on pace to exceed $790 billion, nearly double 2025.
The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index is outperforming the cap-weighted index YTD for the first time since 2022, by ~6%, which the report reads as broadening breadth.
The S&P 500 fell 6% during this earnings season, the weakest earnings season performance since 1Q22.
Weekly cross-asset moves (Thursday to Thursday): WTI crude -7.1%, gold -5.1%, S&P 500 -5.4%, Nasdaq Composite -5.9%, Dow -6.1%, Russell 2000 -5.1%, and the US Dollar Index +0.7%.

sector_views.rationale: Raymond James expects the AI buildout and AI adoption/demand trends to continue, and sees earnings in AI-related areas on solid footing, so the weakness could set up buying opportunities for long-term investors.
The sector is down on average 28% with 58% in a bear market, but earnings remain on solid footing, which Raymond James frames as a potential buying opportunity.
